primitives.name: Angular Relation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Just so the relation of direction between two lines is identical with the peculiar sensation of shape of the space enclosed between them.
primitives.assumptions: Directional relations are intrinsic to perceptual geometry; angular sensation is a topological invariant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When lines are parallel or coincident, angular relation becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Angular relation maps to the topological angle in Euclidean space, isomorphic to the sensory manifold of directional perception.
layer2.telemetry: Perceptual angular deviation from reference frame.

primitives.name: Distance Sensation
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is one more important than the rest, called its distance.
primitives.assumptions: Distance is a fundamental perceptual relation derived from perpendicular projection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Undefined when point lies on the line or in degenerate configurations.

layer2.mapping: Distance kernel emerges from perpendicular projection of point onto line, forming a derived metric space.
layer2.telemetry: Perceptual Euclidean distance from point to line.

primitives.name: Triangularity Sensation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This is the sensation, ideal or actual, of a perpendicular drawn from the point to the line.\ Two lines, one from each extremity of the horizontal to the point, give us a peculiar sensation of triangularity.
primitives.assumptions: Triangularity arises from three-point configuration; perceptual triangle is a topological construct.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates into collinear or singular point configurations.

layer2.mapping: Triangularity sensation corresponds to the area-based topological invariant of the triangle formed by three points.
layer2.telemetry: Perceptual triangle area or angular sum deviation.
